text:
alex: getting multiple support tickets about 5xx + timeouts from hosted inference customers, SLO burn alert fired ~10m ago. p99 latency spiking and gateway returning 502/504s. tickets reference both text-generation and embeddings routes.

maria: saw the SLO alert too. Grafana shows a sudden jump in gateway downstream 504s at 16:12 UTC. p50 unchanged, p95 up a little, p99 huge.

kevin: any deploys around that time?

jamie: Deploys: nothing to inference runtime in the last 24h, but there was a CDN config change at ~15:50 by infra. tagging @maria for correlation.

alex: support-bot forwarded two customer threads — both show requests timing out after ~12s and client-side retries. One includes a curl trace that ends with connection reset.

support-bot: customer ticket #C-9832: "\/v1\/responses returns 502 intermittently, started 16:10 UTC". Attached partial logs.

nate: attaching quick queries I ran:
```
# grafana/logql snippets
sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway",code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (code)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="gateway"}[5m])) by (le))
```

maria: dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/company/gateway-slo?panelId=7 -- you can see probe vs real traffic divergence. probes are fine but real traffic shows high 504.

kevin: that smells like routing / backend connection issue not the runtime. If probes hit different path or use cached routes they skirt the issue.

alex: I suspect the NLB -> gateway node target group had a flapping instance set (we saw unhealthy targets earlier). ops-bot, can you dump target health?

ops-bot: run `infractl elb describe-target-health --tg gateway-prod` or use cloud console. Example output we saw earlier:
```
Instance i-0abc unhealthy, reason: TLSTerminationError
Instance i-0def healthy
```

jamie: confirming, cloud shows 3 targets unhealthy for a short window at 16:11-16:14. That aligns with the SLO burn. But why did TLS termination error show up? no cert rotations scheduled.

nate: I pulled a trace from a failed request (trace id 0x9a7b). It has only client span and gateway entry, missing downstream runtime spans. looks like gateway accepted TCP but never forwarded or dropped the connection. Tracing gap.

maria: sampling rate unchanged. If gateway dropped TCP connections before starting downstream spans, the trace would end early. Need logs from gateway at 16:10-16:16.

alex: pulling logs now: `kubectl -n gateway logs -l app=gateway --since=20m` Relevant lines:
```
2026-03-15T16:12:04Z WARN connection failed handshake: tls: bad record MAC
2026-03-15T16:12:04Z ERROR write to upstream failed: write tcp 10.0.5.12:443: write: connection reset by peer
```

kevin: connection reset by peer + TLS MAC issues could indicate a transient MTU or network path encryption issue, or maybe an edge proxy config change (CDN) at 15:50. Jamie, you said CDN changed headers?

jamie: the CDN tweak was to enable header rewrite for long polls (to fix caching). It should be opt-in and not touch TLS. I can roll it back.

alex: before rollback, can we do quick mitigations: 1) open fallback route to smaller model stack to reduce per-request payload and avoid serialization path, 2) temporarily increase gateway replicas, 3) disable probe filtering so probes follow same path. Which is quickest?

maria: easiest is increase replicas (kubectl scale deployment/gateway --replicas=6). Doing that now.

kevin: I'll flip probe behaviour to use same headers as real traffic (so probes exercise same code path) — will push config in 5m.

nate: support-bot, please add a customer-facing note: "We are investigating elevated timeouts; temporary mitigations in progress. No data loss. Will update in 30 minutes."

support-bot: posted update to the two open tickets.

jamie: rolling CDN header rewrite back now. name: cdn-longpoll-header-rewrite. If this clears TLS errors, we'll know.

alex: monitoring.. p99 decreased slightly after scale + CDN rollback. still intermittent 504s but volume much lower.

maria: logs post-rollback show TLS errors stop at 16:20. Between 16:12-16:20 we had ~8k 5xxs. Post 16:20 we're at baseline.

kevin: conclusion draft: root cause likely mis-applied CDN header rewrite that caused TLS handshake differences at the edge -> backend TLS termination exposed non-standard frames causing 'bad record MAC' and resets. Gateways dropped connections and traces lacked downstream spans. Combined with a small window of unhealthy NLB targets amplified the SLO burn.

alex: action items:
- jamie: postmortem note to infra changelog + revert timeline (done)
- kevin: add integration test that validates TLS handshake invariants after CDN changes (priority P1)
- maria: add alert that correlates probe vs real traffic divergence (current probe pass + real 5xx spike) (P0)
- nate: follow up with customers and confirm mitigation (done)

jamie: I'll open the infra changelog entry and cc security for a quick audit.

kevin: adding a temporary dashboard panel to show trace length distribution (span count per trace) so we can spot dropped downstream spans in future.

support-bot: customers updated. No new tickets in the last 25m for this issue.

alex: closing the incident thread — marking as resolved in 40m if no recurrence. If anyone wants to add notes to the postmortem, please tag `#postmortems` and link the incident id INC-2026-033.

nate: one more note: double-check KMS/HSM rotations not overlapping with CDN changes; odd combo but worth verifying.

jamie: confirmed KMS rotation scheduled next week; not related. Posting incident link now. :white_check_mark:
